# Steve Jobs TV interview about Silicon Valley (1982) 

**Source**: /Volumes/NvME-Satechi/steve-jobs.ai/Database_Steve_Jobs/1980s/Steve Jobs TV interview about Silicon Valley (1982) .mp4

**Transcribed**: 2025-12-31 10:06

---

**Narrator**: Technology makes machines smaller and simpler, changing the way Americans work and play.

**Narrator**: In the 70s, teenagers Steve Jobs and Stephen Wozniak, tinkering in a California garage, invent the circuitry that becomes the brain of the revolutionary Apple computer.

**Steve Jobs**: The penalty for failure, uh, for going and trying to start a company in this valley is non-existent. There really isn't a penalty for failure either psychologically or economically, in the sense that if you have a good idea and you go go out to start your own company, even if you fail, you're generally considered worth more to the company you left because you've gained all this valuable experience in in many disciplines.

**Narrator**: The mushrooming industry gives birth to a new high-tech cult and a place called Silicon Valley.

**Narrator**: Dozens of competitors spring up with new machines, hoping to grab a piece of the rapidly growing market.

**Narrator**: Then, when giant IBM introduces its own personal computer in 1981, the PC world is finally taken seriously.

**Narrator**: Sales skyrocket into the billions of dollars each year.
